Abdul Majid ----- Petitioner

full_judgment: 2. The learned Advocate for the petitioner urges that the courts below committed an error in law in its decision in holding that the pre-emption case is barred by limitation on an erroneous view of section 60 of the Registration Act inasmuch as the case for pre-empting the land was filed on 12.2.85 while the document was registered on 17.11.84. Secondly, he argues that the courts also fell in error in holding that the petitioner is not a contiguous owner of land of plot No. 460. In assailing this finding the learned Advocate drew my attention to the fact that the courts below have found that plot No. 459 is contiguous to plot No. 460 on perusal of mouza map. Therefore, the finding that the plots are not contiguous was made erroneously. I have been taken through the judgment by the learned Advocate. It appears that the court of appeal below while holding that the petitioner's application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 is barred by limitation committed serious error of law in that the case was filed within 4 months from the date of registration under section 60 of the Registration Act on 17.11.84. A transfer is complete on entry in the volume under section 60 and unless that is done there is no transfer as contemplated under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. Limitation in case of a proceeding under section 96 of the Act does not start from the date of execution of the document transferring the land, rather from the date when the document is registered under section 60 of the Registration Act. In this case the document was registered on 17.11.1984 and the pre-emption case was filed on 12.2.1985 in time. The court, it seems to me, equally committed an error in holding that the petitioner is not owner of contiguous plot No. 460 inasmuch as the court itself had found that plot No. 459 and 460 are contiguous to each other on the basis of the mouza map. This finding on evidence is perverse and requires to be aside. So, I set aside the same. The Court below rightly found that the petitioner is a co-sharer by purchase with regard to plot No. 459 in schedule 1 to the plaint. This finding is correct.
